summary.en: Salvadoran missiles and ground forces have struck Haitian gang hideouts, destroying the headquarters of the 400-member Mawozo gang and killing about 20 gang members. Haitian Prime Minister praised President Bukele after the joint strike on the alleged home of a gang leader, and Haitian officials are traveling to El Salvador to discuss the future of the Salvadoran offensive. The United Nations reported that kidnappings in Port-au-Prince rose in the third quarter. The conflict produced 193 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Salvadoranske missiler og bakkestyrker har angrepet haitiske gjengskjul, ødelagt hovedkvarteret til 400‑medlemmer-gjengen Mawozo og drept omtrent 20 gjengmedlemmer. Haitis statsminister roste president Bukele etter det felles angrepet på den påståtte leiren til en gjengleder, og haitiske tjenestemenn reiser til El Salvador for å diskutere fremtiden for den salvadoranske offensiven. FN rapporterte at kidnappinger i Port-au-Prince økte i tredje kvartal. Konflikten førte til 193 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
